title: Advantages and Limitations of TypeScript knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the role of TypeScript in a development workflow?
options: It removes the need for runtime tests.
It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
It replaces the JavaScript runtime in every browser.
It validates all network data automatically.
questions.answer_key: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.explanation: Type checking is a development-time layer and does not replace runtime verification.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Advantages and Limitations of TypeScript”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with type safety and developer productivity and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with type safety and developer productivity and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Type safety and developer productivity”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Advantages and Limitations of TypeScript”?
options: Assume limitations of compile-time guarantees is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check learning and configuration overhead, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check learning and configuration overhead, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Learning and configuration overhead”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
